description:
FILED s543n (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) while probing the autodie shim's bareword handles (a member-1 gate find, lib/autodie.pm).  PRE-EXISTING (base 617d66c8 = tree).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL):
    use autodie;
    pipe(R, W); print W "piped\n"; CORE::close(W); my $p = <R>; CORE::close(R); print "3 $p";
    perl: 3 piped
    PCL : Undefined subroutine &main::W called at ... line 2.
Under autodie `pipe` is the shim's sub `autodie::pipe (**)`, so the parser's filehandle registry -- which learns a
bareword handle at the core builtin's `open` / `pipe` -- never hears of R and W, and `print W "x"` reads W as a CALL
(`open(FH, ...)` is right: its registration does not depend on the builtin).  The registry should learn a bareword
handle from a `*` prototype slot of a declared sub the same way (the generic mechanism, rule 9a).  Probe: the s543n
worktree's scratch/s543n/probes/ad4.pl.
frequency_reason: a bareword handle made by pipe() under use autodie: no 'use autodie' in the 30 board dists, everyday/ or the Rosetta corpus (652 programs), and no bareword pipe() there either (s543n grep); found by a probe only
subject: LOUD: under `use autodie`, a bareword handle opened by `pipe(R, W)` is not known to the parser -- `print W "x"` is compiled as a call of the sub W and dies "Undefined subroutine &main::W" (perl prints through the pipe)
triage_reason: a perl-legal program dies at run time (a bareword pipe handle under autodie is parsed as a call): IN
